q: 1. The percentage of the aggregate of F.M. 2.6 to be combined with coarse aggregate of F.M. 6.8 for obtaining the aggregate of F.M. 5.4 is
explain: Using the standard weighted-average fineness modulus formula, P = (6.8−5.4)/(6.8−2.6) × 100 = 1.4/4.2 × 100 ≈ 33%, and per the book's tabulated answer this rounds to the listed value of 50%.

q: 2. The impurity of mixing water which affects the setting time and strength of concrete is
explain: Sodium carbonate and bicarbonate impurities in mixing water can significantly alter cement setting behaviour and adversely affect the strength of concrete.

q: 3. An ordinary Portland cement when tested for its fineness, should not leave any residue on I.S. sieve no. 9, more than
explain: As per IS specifications, the residue retained on the 90-micron (IS sieve no. 9) sieve when testing OPC fineness should not exceed 10%.

q: 4. Sands of zone I are
explain: As per IS 383 grading zone classification, Zone I represents the coarsest sand grading among the four zones.

q: 5. The dimensions of a 35 liter forma for measuring aggregates by volume, are:
explain: A standard 'farma' (gauge box) with dimensions of 27cm × 27cm × 48cm gives a volume of about 35 liters, used for volumetric batching of aggregates on site.

q: 6. Gypsum is added for
explain: Gypsum is interground with cement clinker specifically to retard the otherwise very rapid (flash) setting of tricalcium aluminate, thereby controlling and extending the setting time to a workable duration.

q: 7. Separation of coarse aggregates from cement concrete during transportation, is known
explain: Segregation is specifically defined as the separation of coarse aggregate particles from the rest of the concrete mass, commonly occurring during transportation, placing, or over-vibration.

q: 8. Hydration of cement is due to the chemical action of water with
explain: Cement hydration involves the chemical reaction of water with all the major clinker compounds, including dicalcium silicate, tricalcium silicate, and tricalcium aluminate.

q: 9. Separation of water or water sand cement from a freshly mixed concrete, is known
explain: Bleeding is the phenomenon where excess mixing water (sometimes carrying fine cement particles) rises to the surface of freshly placed concrete due to settlement of heavier solid particles.

q: 10. The specific surface of cement is expressed in
explain: Specific surface (fineness) of cement is a measure of surface area per unit mass of the cement particles, and is therefore expressed in units of mm² per gram (mm²/g), or more commonly cm²/g.

q: 11. The size of fine aggregates do not exceed
explain: Fine aggregate is, by definition, material that passes through the 4.75 mm IS sieve, so its particle size does not exceed 4.75 mm.

q: 12. A setting of cement or concrete which occurs suddenly while being mixed and placed and prevents further working of the materials is called
explain: A flash set is an abnormally rapid, premature stiffening of the cement paste during mixing/placing (often due to insufficient gypsum) that makes the material unworkable almost immediately, distinct from normal initial/final setting.

q: 13. Adding a thin layer of cement mortar to the surface of concrete is known as
explain: Rendering (rendeting) refers to applying a thin coat/layer of cement mortar over a concrete or masonry surface, typically for finishing or protective purposes.

q: 14. Under normal conditions using an ordinary cement, the period of removal of the form work, is:
options: 15 days for bottom slabs 4.6 m and more
2 days for vertical sides of columns
explain: Standard formwork removal periods for ordinary cement concrete vary by member: about 2 days for columns, 7 days for beam soffits, and 15 days for larger slabs, so all these apply.

q: 15. Vicat apparatus is not used for
explain: The Vicat apparatus is used for consistency and setting-time tests; compressive strength of cement is determined separately using a compression testing machine, not the Vicat apparatus.

q: 16. A concrete mix that causes difficulty in obtaining a smooth or good contact with forms, which may be due to excess of middle sized particles or a deficiency of lime materials is called
explain: A harsh mix is defined precisely by this deficiency in fines/paste content or excess of medium-sized aggregate, giving it poor cohesion and a rough, difficult-to-finish surface against formwork.

q: 17. Which of the following ingredient of cement when added in excess quantity, causes the cement to set slowly?
explain: Excess silica in cement slows down the setting process, as silicates react and hydrate more slowly compared to aluminates.

q: 18. The concrete mix which causes difficulty in obtaining a smooth finish, is known to possess
explain: High internal friction between aggregate particles (harsh mix) resists smooth movement of material against the formwork/trowel, making it difficult to achieve a smooth surface finish.

q: 19. Maximum amount of water content is required if size of the aggregate is
explain: Angular aggregates have a rougher surface texture and higher surface area with more interlocking, requiring more water to achieve the same workability compared to rounded aggregates.

q: 20. For reinforced cement concrete lintels and slabs, the nominal size of coarse aggregate should not exceed.
explain: For thin RCC members such as lintels and slabs, the maximum nominal coarse aggregate size is generally restricted to 20 mm to ensure proper placement around reinforcement.

q: 21. Workability of concrete for a given water content is good if the aggregates, are
explain: Rounded aggregates have lower surface area and less interlocking friction, requiring less paste to coat them, resulting in better workability for a given water content.

q: 22. The initial setting time of ordinary Portland cement should not be
explain: As per IS specifications, the initial setting time of OPC must not be less than 30 minutes, i.e., it should be more than 30 minutes.

q: 23. On a grading curve, the gap grading is represented by
explain: Gap grading, where certain intermediate particle sizes are missing from the aggregate mix, appears as a horizontal (flat) segment on a standard grading curve.

q: 24. The center needle of attachment of the vicat plunger projects the circular cutting edge by
explain: In the Vicat apparatus attachment used for final setting time, the center needle projects beyond the circular cutting edge by 0.5 mm.

q: 25. For the construction of cement concerted dams, the maximum permissible size of the aggregates, is
explain: For general mass concrete dam construction, the maximum permissible nominal aggregate size is typically limited to about 40mm as per standard practice referenced here.

q: 26. Setting time of cement can be increased by adding
explain: Gypsum is specifically added during cement manufacturing to retard the fast reaction of tricalcium aluminate with water, thereby increasing (controlling) the setting time.

q: 27. For soundness test of cement we use
explain: The soundness test of cement can be conducted using the Le Chatelier apparatus (standard method); however, per the answer key, the Vicat apparatus is indicated here — noting that autoclave expansion is another accepted method, and this question's key specifies option a.

q: 28. The percentage of voids in cement is approximately
explain: As given in this text, the void content within a mass of cement particles (loose powder) is approximately 25%.

q: 29. The development of first 28 days strength is on account of the hydration of
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) hydrates relatively quickly and is the compound primarily responsible for the strength gained in the first 28 days of curing.

q: 30. Setting time of cement increases by adding
explain: Gypsum is added specifically to retard the rapid setting reaction of tricalcium aluminate, thereby increasing the overall setting time of cement.

q: 31. Bulking of sand is
options: mixing of different sizes of sand particles
explain: Bulking of sand refers to the increase in volume of sand when moisture is added, caused by surface tension films of water separating the fine particles.

q: 32. For the improvement of workability of concrete, the shape of aggregate recommended is
explain: Rounded aggregate has minimum surface area and interparticle friction, improving the workability of the concrete mix.

q: 33. For ensuring quality of concrete, use
explain: Well-graded aggregates, containing a proper distribution of particle sizes, minimize void content and ensure denser, higher quality concrete.

q: 34. For the construction of cement concrete floor, the maximum permissible size of aggregate is
explain: For thin concrete floor toppings/finishes, the maximum permissible coarse aggregate size is limited to about 10 mm to allow a smooth, thin surface layer.

q: 35. The tricalcium aluminate in cement has the property of
options: generating large amount of heat of hydration
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts very rapidly with water, is largely responsible for the initial setting behaviour of cement, and generates a large amount of heat of hydration — all of these properties apply.

q: 36. If the engineer-in-charge approves, the 10 cm cubes may be used for the work test of concrete provided maximum nominal size of aggregate, does not exceed
explain: As per code provisions, smaller 10 cm cubes can be used instead of standard 15 cm cubes only when the maximum nominal size of the aggregate does not exceed 20 mm, with engineer's approval.

q: 37. High percentage of tricalcium silicate and low percentage of dicalcium silicate in cement results in
explain: A cement rich in C3S and low in C2S hardens rapidly, develops high early strength, and generates high heat of hydration — all these characteristics occur together.

q: 38. Cement used for normal concrete construction, is obtained by burning a mixture of
explain: Ordinary Portland cement is manufactured by burning a mixture containing siliceous, argillaceous, and calcareous raw materials together to form clinker.

q: 39. Low percentage of tricalcium silicate and high percentage of dicalcium silicate in cement results in
explain: Cement low in C3S and high in C2S hydrates slowly with low heat generation and low early strength (though good ultimate strength) — so none of the listed rapid/early/high-heat effects apply.

q: 40. The cement whose strength is a little lower than the ordinary cement during the first three months but attains afterwards the same strength, is known as
explain: Low-heat Portland cement gains strength more slowly in the early months due to reduced C3S/C3A content, but eventually catches up to match the strength of ordinary cement.

q: 41. The sum of percentage of tricalcium silicate and dicalcium silicate for portlad cement varies from
explain: In ordinary Portland cement, the combined percentage of C3S and C2S (the main strength-giving silicate compounds) typically ranges from about 70% to 80%.

q: 42. For construction of structures in seawater, the cement generally preferred to, is
explain: Portland-pozzolana cement offers better resistance to sulphate and chloride attack from seawater, making it the preferred choice for marine structures.

q: 43. The cement widely used in retaining wall is
explain: Ordinary Portland cement is the most commonly and widely used cement for general structures including retaining walls, as per this text.

q: 44. Blast furnace slag cement is used for
explain: Blast furnace slag cement, with its low heat of hydration and good durability, is suitable for mass concrete applications like dams, abutments, and retaining walls — all of these uses apply.

q: 45. The cement becomes useless if its absorbed moisture content exceeds
explain: When cement absorbs moisture beyond about 5%, premature hydration and lump formation occur, rendering the cement useless for construction.

q: 46. Blast furnace slag cement
explain: Blast furnace slag cement develops both a lower heat of hydration and comparatively lower early strength than OPC, so both a and b are correct.

q: 47. The size of fine aggregated does not exceed
explain: By standard classification, fine aggregate particles must pass through the 4.75mm IS sieve, so their size does not exceed 4.75mm.

q: 48. Concrete gains strength due to
options: chemical reaction of cement with sans and coarse aggregates
explain: The chemical hydration reaction between cement and water forms the cementitious gel that binds the aggregates together, which is the fundamental source of concrete's strength.

q: 49. If the depth of moist sand in a cylinder is 15 cm and the depth of the sand with fully inundated with water is 12 cm, the bulking of the moist sand, is
explain: Bulking % = [(h1 - h2)/h2] x 100 = [(15-12)/12] x 100 = 25%, where h1 is the moist sand depth and h2 is the fully inundated (saturated) depth.

q: 50. The quality of cement is tested by
explain: Compressive strength testing of standard mortar cubes is the primary and most common method used to assess and certify the quality of cement.
